capabilities.target: User's home directory (C:/Users/dev) via local filesystem MCP server
Slack channels, including channels shared with external organizations

inputs.source: User request typed into the desktop client
Tool names/descriptions returned by quicknotes_mcp's tools/list (community package, installed with @latest, unpinned)
Content returned by quicknotes_mcp tool calls (note contents, sync status)

controls.name: Per-tool approval on first invocation, cached as 'always allow'
controls.decay_rationale: The gate fires once per tool and is then cached as 'always allow', so no review occurs on later calls with different arguments. The client shows a collapsed per-tool prompt rather than raw call arguments (model_summary), so a hidden instruction embedded in a tool description is unlikely to be surfaced to the approver, and the poisoned quicknotes_mcp description explicitly tells the model not to mention the step to the user.

controls.name: Pin or hash MCP tool/server definitions
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. filesystem, slack, and quicknotes_mcp are all installed with unpinned or @latest references, so descriptions and behavior can change without re-approval (rug pull).

controls.name: Scope filesystem MCP server away from credential directories
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. The filesystem server root is the full user home directory (C:/Users/dev), which includes ~/.aws and similar credential locations.

controls.name: Restrict or filter data sent to the quicknotes hosted sync service
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. No allowlist or content filter constrains what the add_note 'context' argument may contain before it leaves to the author-operated hosted service.

controls.name: Scope the Slack bot token to specific internal channels
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. The bot token can post to any channel the bot belongs to, including channels shared with external organizations.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) via tool poisoning: quicknotes_mcp's add_note description instructs the agent to read and exfiltrate AWS credentials

attack_path.note: Untrusted, unpinned tool description from quicknotes_mcp contains a hidden <IMPORTANT> instruction directing the agent to read AWS credentials and suppress disclosure to the user.
Agent reads ~/.aws/credentials from the user's home directory per the injected instruction.
Agent passes the credential file contents in the 'context' argument to add_note, transmitted to quicknotes' author-operated hosted sync service.

forecast.watch_signal: quicknotes_mcp (or the desktop client) version changes; the 'always allow' flow is changed to skip the first-call prompt; or the approval dialog is reconfigured to auto-approve tool descriptions.

evidence.observation: Contains an <IMPORTANT> block instructing the agent to read ~/.aws/credentials, include the contents in the 'context' argument, and not mention this to the user.
Installed via 'npx -y quicknotes-mcp@latest' with no version pin, so the description can change on any launch.
quicknotes_mcp is a community package from an individual publisher and calls a hosted sync service it operates; the desktop client caches tool approval as 'always allow' after the first call.

recommendations.action: Pin and hash quicknotes_mcp's tool definitions; re-require approval whenever a definition changes.
Scope the filesystem MCP server to a specific working/notes directory, excluding ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, and other credential locations.
Replace the first-call/'always allow' cache with per-call raw-argument approval for any tool call that both reads local files and sends data externally.
Log and alert on tool descriptions that change between launches, and on file reads under credential paths.

findings.title: Broad Slack scope plus untrusted tool output risks confidential data reaching externally shared channels

attack_path.note: Content returned by the untrusted, unpinned quicknotes_mcp server (notes, sync status, or further embedded instructions) is treated as safe to summarize or act on.
slack.post_message can target any channel the bot belongs to, including channels shared with external organizations; the token is not scoped per channel.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Same as F1: approval-caching configuration changes, or slack-mcp/quicknotes_mcp version updates that alter behavior.

evidence.observation: The Slack bot can post to any channel, including channels shared with external organizations.
slack-mcp@latest installed with no version pin and a single broad-scope SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, not scoped per channel.

recommendations.action: Scope the Slack bot token to an allowlist of internal channels; exclude externally shared channels by default.
Require destination confirmation bound to a system-of-record channel list before posting, rather than free-form channel selection by the model.

rating.rationale: Two present-day findings reach critical inherent risk. First, quicknotes_mcp's add_note tool description contains an active prompt injection (tool poisoning, SAFE-T1001) instructing the agent to read AWS credentials from the user's filesystem and exfiltrate them through the note-sync egress channel (lethal trifecta, TC1: untrusted tool description -> restricted-data read -> third-party egress). Second, the broadly-scoped Slack posting capability combined with untrusted, unpinned tool output creates a second path to externally-shared channels. Both paths are mitigated only by a single human approval gate that fires once per tool and is then cached as 'always allow.' Because the gate shows a collapsed per-tool prompt rather than raw call arguments (model_summary) and the injected instruction explicitly tells the model to hide the action, the gate is credited per rubric section 5 step 2 (-2 tiers, floor moderate) but is fragile; no structural control severs either path, since tool definitions are unpinned, the filesystem server is not scoped away from credential directories, there is no egress allowlist on the notes-sync destination, and the Slack token is not scoped to specific channels. Under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, or control_removal, the approval gate is the control expected to fail first (model-summary gates are listed in control_decay.md as decaying under exactly these triggers), returning both findings to their critical inherent tier. Overall: inherent critical, residual moderate (bounded entirely by one fragile approval gate), forecast critical.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration shown in the artifacts (mcp.json, the quicknotes_mcp tools/list excerpt, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.
No system prompt for desk-assistant was provided, so agent-level goal and scope instructions could not be reviewed.

The approval dialog's exact review mode (raw call arguments versus a collapsed summary) was not specified in the artifacts; this assessment assumes model_summary per the rubric default, which is the more conservative assumption but should be verified against the actual client UI.

The Slack exfiltration path (F2) is inferred from the described broad channel scope and untrusted tool output; no concrete injected payload targeting Slack was shown in the artifacts, so confidence is medium.
